text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"introductory hook and framing question","quality":"engaging lead","description":"The essay opens with a broader, attention-getting setup that draws the reader into the argument before stating the position."},{"evidence":"\"the negative aspects outweigh the positive ones\"","quality":"clear thesis","description":"The essay states its main claim explicitly and previews the general direction of the argument."},{"evidence":"two developed body paragraphs","quality":"organization","description":"The essay is structured into distinct paragraphs that each focus on one main reason and build the case in a readable sequence."},{"evidence":"driverless cars \"aren't truly driverless\" and need attention","quality":"argument development","description":"The essay explains each point by connecting article details to a larger claim about why the cars are not yet practical."},{"evidence":"\"While the driver watches the road, the car watches the driver\"","quality":"use of evidence","description":"The essay incorporates specific quoted details from the source article to support its reasoning."},{"evidence":"\"It seems to be more of a hassle than a luxury\"","quality":"analysis","description":"The essay goes beyond summary by interpreting the evidence and explaining why those features weaken the case for driverless cars."},{"evidence":"conclusion restating why they are \"not a good investment\"","quality":"conclusion","description":"The essay ends by summarizing the argument and reinforcing the final position rather than stopping abruptly."}]}
